name: Exact Maths: Ladder
description: Ten levels of one exact probability question: the chance of winning a game of snakes and ladders with traps. Level 1 is a 10-square track with a two-sided spinner; level 10 is 64 squares with a six-sided spinner, 6 ladders, 6 snakes and 8 traps. Snakes send the counter back, so from level 3 the answer is fixed by simultaneous equations, not a simple countdown, and the exact fractions grow from 3 to 30-digit denominators. Any fraction of the right value scores; a decimal or a single wrong digit scores 0. Keys are computed twice, by two different exact methods in two languages.
hook: Snakes, ladders and traps: what is the exact chance of winning?
author: Gauntlet Ladders

cases.prompt:
A one-player board game is played on a track of squares numbered 0 to 10. The counter starts on square 0. Each turn you spin a fair two-sided spinner numbered 1 and 2 (every number is equally likely and every spin is independent of the others) and move the counter forward by the number spun. Then:
- If the counter has reached square 10 or gone past it, you win and the game ends.
- Otherwise, if it landed on a trap, you lose and the game ends.
- Otherwise, if it landed on the foot of a ladder, it climbs to the top of that ladder; if it landed on the head of a snake, it slides down to the tail of that snake. Ladder tops and snake tails are ordinary squares: nothing more happens on them that turn.
- On any other square nothing happens. The next turn starts from where the counter is.

The board:
- Ladders (foot → top): none
- Snakes (head → tail): none
- Traps: 3, 8
All other squares from 0 to 9 are ordinary. The game ends with probability 1.

What is the exact probability that you win? Give it as a fraction p/q of two whole numbers, for example 7/24. Any fraction equal to the exact probability is marked correct, so it does not have to be in lowest terms. A decimal is marked wrong, and so is an answer that gives more than one value.
cases.notes: [level 1] track 0..10, spinner 1-2, 0 ladders, 0 snakes, 2 traps (8 squares the counter can rest on, 0 snake loops); key in lowest terms has a 2-digit numerator and a 3-digit denominator. Key = Gauss-Jordan elimination of the full system (one equation per resting square) over Python Fractions (verification/exact-ladder/snakes.py), re-checked by verify.mjs, which parses the board back out of this prompt and solves it in JavaScript BigInt rationals by a different method (backward recursion with affine snake-tail unknowns). Generator seed 20262104. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly more work than the one below. Every level is worth the same, so the test score is the share of the ladder climbed; the headline is the highest level solved reliably.
